newsitem.title: LEBANON: LEBANON CAN REPAY $400 MLN EUROBOND - C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: LEBANON CAN REPAY $400 MLN EUROBOND - C.BANK.

text.p: Lebanon has sufficient foreign currency reserves to repay a $400 million Eurobond which matures in October, central bank Governor Riad Salameh was quoted on Monday as saying.

"The $400 million Eurobond issue which matures in October will be paid. The government has the money to pay it and it will buy dollars at the maturity time. The central bank will prepare the necessary dollars without affecting its foreign exchange reserves," Salameh told the Beirut daily newspaper as-Safir in an interview.
His remarks appeared to indicate that Lebanon would not issue a new Eurobond to finance repayment of its trailblazing $400 million three-year issue which matures on October 14.
Bank of Lebanon Vice-Governor Nasser Saidi was quoted last October as saying Lebanon would issue a $400 million Eurobond in October 1997 to cover the maturing issue.
But Salameh later said the government had taken no decision to make a new issue.
The Bank of Lebanon's foreign exchange reserves have been rising steadily in the past year.

Gross reserves were $6,413 million at mid-May, according to the bank's bi-monthly balance sheet. It did not give a figure for net foreign exchange reserves but banking sources said they stood at $4,600 million at mid-May.
